desk_requests.question: Answer to your M3.12 (Answer to your M2.6 (Can a script pull LITE and COHR one-month daily returns and report their pairwise correlation? The deterministic redundancy screen returned): [held] Verdict unchanged and now measured rather than argued: LITE/COHR stays `redundant`, keep LITE, drop COHR. Your numbers strengthen it on the right test -- the pair correlates more tightly with each other (0.843 / 21s, 0.891 / 63s) than either does with SMH (0.789 / 0.819) or with the third optics name GLW (0.791 / 0.821), so this is pair-specific co-movement, not shared sector beta being double-counted. I will state the caveat honestly rather than overclaim: the excess over sector beta is roughly 7-10pp, not the 40-50pp you would see in a share-class pair, so LITE/COHR is a high-overlap pair sitting on top of an already high common factor, not a duplicate listing.
